item.title: Alan Patrick set for his smallest role at Inter since returning
item.description: Alan Patrick set for his smallest role at Inter since returning A doubt for next Tuesday’s (3rd) clash with Coritiba, midfielder Alan Patrick finds himself in an unusual situation in 2026. This season is on course to be his quietest in terms of appearances, minutes played and goal contributions, counting only the years in which he played a full season for Internacional, according to data compiled by ge. The No. 10 caused concern among fans when he was substituted in the 88th minute of the defeat to Fluminense, a match in which he scored. After feeling pain in his right thigh, the player will undergo a further medical assessment to determine his fitness for the next round of fixtures. So far, Alan Patrick has featured in 40 of Inter’s 51 matches in 2026, totaling 2,899 minutes. His nine goals and eight assists fall short of his figures for 2023, 2024 and 2025, according to ge. It is worth noting that the analysis considers only full seasons, as the player arrived at Beira-Rio midway through 2022. Despite the decline in his numbers, the captain’s influence remains undeniable. He is tied as the squad’s second-highest scorer this year alongside Borré—who is no longer at the club—and Vitinho, all with nine goals, behind only Bernabei’s 10. Alan Patrick is also the team’s leading provider, topping the assists chart outright. The new tactical approach and the captain’s role Regarded as one of the dressing-room leaders and the squad’s standout technical talent, Alan Patrick struggled at the start of the year. Under Paulo Pezzolano, Internacional adopted a more reactive tactical approach in the Brasileirão. With a system focused on physicality and defensive work, the classic No. 10’s style fell out of favor, costing him his place in the starting lineup. The midfielder endured five consecutive matches on the bench without even being called upon by the Uruguayan coach. Recently, however, the situation has taken a turn. With Eduardo Baptista’s arrival as head coach, Alan Patrick has regained a central role and started four of the last five matches, repaying that trust with two goals and an assist. One curious detail concerns Inter’s record in the Brazilian Championship. In six matches without their captain on the pitch, Inter recorded four wins (against Santos, Corinthians, Fluminense and Vasco) and just two defeats (against Cruzeiro and Mirassol). By contrast, in the 27 league matches in which Alan Patrick featured, the team registered four wins, 11 draws and 12 defeats. This article was translated into English by Artificial Intelligence. You can read the original version in 🇧🇷 here.

item.title: 2027: Stick to your timetable, APC urges INEC
item.description: To take advantage of 13m members, 31 governors, 88 senators, 208 Reps. Demands equal media access, venues for all parties By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The ruling All Progressives Congress APC has urged the Independent National Electoral Commission INEC to adhere strictly to its published timetable for the 2027 general elections, insisting that the rules must apply equally to every political party. APC national chairman, Prof. Nentawe Goshwe Yilwatda, made the demand while receiving a pre-election fact-finding mission of the Economic Community of West African States ECOWAS at the party’s National Secretariat in Abuja. Special Adviser to the National Chairman on Media and Information Strategy, Mr Abimbola Tooki, in a statement on Sunday in Abuja, said Yilwatda received the mission, led by former Vice-President of Sierra Leone, Victor Bockarie Foh, with members of the National Working Committee NWC. “We believe INEC should stick to its timetable. The rules must apply equally to every political party. The electoral process must be fair, transparent and predictable, without adjusting deadlines in a manner that gives any party an undue advantage,” Yilwatda said. He said the APC had already released its campaign council list, inaugurated the council, commenced campaign activities and uploaded its candidates to the INEC portal ahead of its rivals. According to him, the party has presented candidates for all the elective positions it is contesting, in contrast to the difficulties some opposition parties reportedly encountered in fielding candidates and completing their submission processes. He said APC’s organisational strength placed it ahead of other parties. “Our party is the largest political party in Nigeria. In terms of structure, organisation and membership, no other political party comes close to us. We are approximately three times larger than the next political party in the country,” he said. He disclosed that the party has approximately 13 million registered members in all local government areas, with membership identity cards designed to allow verification through their National Identification Numbers NIN and voter identification details. The chairman added that the APC has more than 261,000 executive members across its structures from the ward to the national level. On elected offices, he said the party has 31 governors out of 36, 88 senators out of the 109-member Senate, and 208 members of the House of Representatives out of 360 seats. He added that the party also has a significant presence in state Houses of Assembly. “These structures are the foundation of our strength. We have built an organisation that reaches every part of the country and gives us the capacity to engage Nigerians across different demographics,” he said. Yilwatda said more than 7,000 aspirants contested for various positions in the party’s primaries, yet it recorded relatively few post-primary court cases compared with the scale of the contests. item.title: Atiku tackles APC over Tinubu’s power pledge, says bonds can’t light homes
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has challenged the All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council, APC-PCC, over its defence of President Bola Tinubu’s electricity pledge, insisting that Nigerians cannot power their homes and businesses with laws, bonds and project announcements. Atiku said despite the administration’s explanations about reforms and ongoing projects, Nigerians were still battling unreliable electricity, rising tariffs and the cost of alternative power, three and a half years after Tinubu promised steady supply and an end to estimated billing. In a statement on Sunday by the Director of Strategic Communication of the African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council, ADC-PCC, Phrank Shaibu, the former vice president accused the APC campaign council of celebrating policy documents and financial interventions instead of addressing the failure to translate them into reliable electricity. “The APC should spare Nigerians the spectacle of celebrating paperwork while homes and businesses remain in darkness. After three and a half years, families still struggle to keep their homes lit. Traders and small business owners spend scarce resources on alternative power, yet struggle to keep their businesses alive. Nigerians are billed for electricity they cannot rely on. President Tinubu promised steady power and an end to estimated billing. That promise has not been kept,” he said. Atiku also faulted the electricity band system, arguing that consumers were paying different tariffs without corresponding improvements in supply. He cited Band A tariffs of about N209.50 per unit in many areas, before VAT, to illustrate the burden on consumers, insisting that Nigerians across all five bands continued to pay for electricity they could not reliably access. “No family should have to weigh the cost of electricity against the cost of food. No business should be left to pay more while receiving less,” he said. The former vice president also demanded clarity on the Federal Government’s plan to end electricity subsidies from 2027, questioning what the move would mean for household and business electricity bills. He proposed working with state governments and regulators to abolish the existing band system and introduce what he described as a fairer, more affordable framework that would hold power companies accountable for electricity delivered. Atiku’s lampooned the administration’s multitrillion-naira bond programme to settle legacy debts owed to generation companies, which he said could not be mistaken for investment in new electricity generation infrastructure. He alleged that the Tinubu administration had not built any new generation infrastructure of its own to expand Nigeria’s power capacity. “Paying old debts is not the same as building new power infrastructure. item.title: A NU START
item.description: Oct 31, 2026; University Park, Pennsylvania, USA; Penn State Nittany Lions running back Cam Wallace (26) runs with the ball while avoiding a tackle by Purdue Boilermakers linebacker Jojo Hayden (0) during the fourth quarter of the game at West Shore Home Field at Beaver Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Matthew O'Haren-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Penn State is finally on the win column. The Nittany Lions, down both Chase Sowell and Koby Howard, managed to use the run game to actually beat a Purdue team that quite a few folks thought would give Penn State problems, if not win outright. The Nittany Lions used the bye week to make adjustments to the offense, and Cam Wallace seems to have taken full advantage of those adjustments, to the tune of 135 yards on the ground. Both teams scored in the first quarter. Rocco Becht threw a 4-yard touchdown pass to Andrew Rappleyea. Ryan Browne answered with a 33-yard touchdown pass to Xavier Townsend, and the game was tied 7-7. Becht then ran for a 6-yard touchdown. Replay review upheld the call. Penn State led 14-7 after one quarter. The second quarter featured a special teams play for Purdue. Bisi Owens blocked a Penn State punt, and Jalil Hall recovered it and scored. The game was tied 14-14. Carson Hansen then ran for a 1-yard touchdown with 1:50 left in the half. Penn State led 21-14 at halftime. The third quarter had one score. Ryan Barker kicked a 44-yard field goal, and Penn State led 24-14 heading into the fourth. Penn State closed out the game in the fourth quarter. Cam Wallace ran for a 2-yard touchdown, which made it 31-14. Purdue’s Jacobo Echeverria Lozano kicked a 49-yard field goal for the final score of 31-17. Penn State, moving forward, has a chance to redefine their season. They could use this win as a springboard for the remaining four games, having a win under their belt and the experience of taking over a game. Next up, a trip to Washington. Good luck. Stats and Storylines 269 – Rushing yards against Purdue. That’s good for second most on the season, behind the 304 against Buffalo. 175 – Yards allowed by the defense. What a difference a bye week makes! 1:14 – Amount of time Purdue possessed the ball in the second quarter. Oof! Highlights

item.title: Colandrea Passes on the Press Conference after the Offense Passed on Scoring Points – The Morning After
item.description: First things first. If you are the starting quarterback at Nebraska and you just re-signed for another year for allegedly $6 million, then you come out to the press conference and take some arrows for your team. Moving On. We all knew last night was coming and that is the problem with this football program. Nebraska’s defense completely dominated the game, but just like against Indiana, it was two plays the defense surrendered which made all the difference. We should not require the Nebraska defense to play perfectly in order to win football games against teams like Washington. Earlier this week Dana Holgorsen said that it felt like it was a race to 21 points in order to win a Big Ten football game. He made it about one-third of the way. It is almost ironic and comical that after the report about Nebraska re-signing Anthony Colandrea for next year, he then throws two interceptions in his first three passes of the game. It was like we should have expected it. Anthony Colandrea was not the only problem. The entire offense was the problem last night. Whenever there were a few steps forward then we would see several steps back. Whether it was drops or extremely badly timed penalties on big gains (which has happened all year). Or when Nebraska gets away from running the ball with the running backs. This is probably the best defense we have seen since the Pelini years. This offense is ruining a potentially program-changing season in front of them. Nebraska had a great opportunity to be 8-2. They were favored by 7.5 or 8.5. They dominated the game for nearly 3.75 quarters. However, again, the problem is that Nebraska fans knew what was coming. They knew exactly what was going to happen. It felt inevitable. I was saying during the entire second half that the Nebraska defense was going to have to get a turnover or a score for Nebraska to win and it didn’t happen. The Morning After Steven Sipple: Nebraska falls for third straight time, and it again feels nightmarish “Welcome to Your Worst Nightmare.” That’s what the banner in Nebraska’s student section cautioned Saturday night at Memorial Stadium, aimed at the visiting Washington Huskies. This was a nightmare, all right. For the home team. What we learned from Nebraska’s loss to Washington Nebraska had yet another golden opportunity to kickstart the second half of its season. For the third straight game, it suffered another brutal defeat. Here are our five biggest takeaways from the Huskers’ 17-10 loss to Washington and what it means for head coach Matt Rhule and Co. going forward… Rhule postgame comments after Huskers lose it again in the fourth quarter It feels the same, but there’s always some odd road taken to this dark place. This week’s strange, haunting path included a fourth-and-18 conversion by Washington when one stop by the Blackshirts would’ve basically won it. But of course. Third straight Nebraska collapse sends once-promising season into tailspin LINCOLN, Neb. — Not again. Yes, again. Nebras

item.title: Ole Gunnar Solskjaer insists Michael Carrick is the right man for Manchester United and reveals his own offer to return
item.description: Fenerbahce v Besiktas - Turkish Super League - Getty Images Sport Ole Gunnar Solskjaer insists Michael Carrick is still the right man to take Manchester United forward, despite a nine-game winless run that has left them 17th in the Premier League. Solskjaer also revealed he offered to step in after Ruben Amorim's sacking in January, but spoke highly of Carrick, his former assistant, when the club were weighing up their options. Solskjaer backs Carrick despite winless run Carrick's side slipped to a 2-0 defeat at Chelsea on Saturday, as Morgan Rogers struck shortly after half-time and Cole Palmer converted a penalty after Lisandro Martinez was sent off. United are now without a win in nine games, their longest such run since 1988, and sit 17th in the Premier League. Solskjaer, however, remains firmly in Carrick's corner. Speaking to Norwegian outlet TV2, he said: "Michael has what it takes to take that club forward. I think he's the right man. He understands the club, understands the fans, and knows what's required. You don't see that 'devil' in him. But it's there, and I have it too. We are so incredibly alike." Solskjaer recommended Carrick to United chiefs Carrick, who played alongside Solskjaer at Old Trafford and later worked as his assistant, was named caretaker boss after Amorim's sacking in January. He was then handed the job permanently after guiding United to third place and Champions League qualification, and Solskjaer revealed he had put in a good word for his former team-mate. "Perhaps not many people thought I would become a football coach, certainly not the manager of Manchester United. Many probably thought the same about Michael Carrick," he said. "When I spoke with United, I also spoke highly of Michael. 'If you choose him, you're getting a good man,' I said. I believe he did the same for me. Neither of us was desperate to get the job. But we'd likely step up if they asked." Solskjaer offered to step in after Amorim exit Solskjaer, who spent three years in charge of United before leaving in 2021, was linked with a return after an unsuccessful spell at Besiktas last season. He confirmed he held talks with the club's hierarchy in January, saying: "I had a good chat with Jason Wilcox and Omar Berrada. We didn't discuss contract length or anything of the sort. I offered to step in if needed, and I made no demands. I shared my thoughts on what is required for the club to move forward. We had one brief conversation. There were no negotiations." Reflecting on his time at the club, Solskjaer added: "There were some fantastic moments, but everything has its time. I do miss it, yes. I could have imagined staying there forever, but life goes on. It was a very special period. Of course it was. It was special in many ways. Going back to the past isn't always a good idea. item.title: Braves predicted to trade Ronald Acuna Jr. for Phillies' $330M two-time MVP in monster deal
item.description: Braves predicted to trade Ronald Acuna Jr. for Phillies' $330M two-time MVP in monster deal originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Atlanta Braves are entering another crucial offseason after it became clear that their starting rotation wasn't deep enough when it came time for the postseason. The starting pitchers were great, but having to rely on a bullpen game every third game shouldn't be the norm in the playoffs. Now, the Braves have several important decisions to make that could shape the future of the organization. One of those decisions was whether to bring Ozzie Albies and Ronald Acuña Jr. back. On Friday, Atlanta announced that both players would return for the 2027 season. “The Braves today exercised options for OF Ronald Acuña Jr. and INF Ozzie Albies for the 2027 season,” the Braves posted. However, that doesn't mean Acuña is entirely off the trade market. His lack of production as a former MVP has disappointed fans and raised questions about whether Atlanta could move him. Bleacher Report's Zachary D. Rymer believes the Braves could trade Acuña for Philadelphia Phillies superstar Bryce Harper in a blockbuster deal. “Anyway, the rationale starts here: Bryce Harper should probably move on from Philadelphia, and Ronald Acuña Jr. should probably do the same from Atlanta. Things for both players in both places have gotten…weird. So, why not swap the two players? The obvious answer is "Because they're NL East rivals, you fool," and that is fair. Even so, the shoe fits on both ends. The Phillies need youth and a right-handed bat, and the Braves need more present upside than Acuña has shown over the last two years,” Rymer wrote. Harper is starting to feel the pressure as he continues to chase a World Series title in Philadelphia. The two-time MVP did mention that the roster could look different in 2027. “I'd imagine this team is going to look a lot different next year," Harper said. This would be one of the wildest trades in MLB history, as division rivals rarely trade superstars with each other. However, it is a move that could potentially benefit both teams. The biggest obstacle is Harper's $330 million contract with the Phillies . Atlanta typically isn't eager to take on massive contracts, but for a blockbuster swap like this, the potential payoff might make it worth considering. item.title: Cowboys vs Cardinals live updates: Score, highlights, predictions, analysis
item.description: The Dallas Cowboys were able to stop their two-game losing streak in Week 7, heading to Philadelphia and leaving their Monday night matchup with a resounding 38-21 win. Can they parlay that victory into a winning streak? To do so, they'll have to get rid of the pesky Arizona Cardinals , who despite being a lackluster organization for the better part of the their recent history, have owned the Cowboys, winning eight of the last nine matchups. That includes a matchup last season that saw Jacoby Brissett own the day against Matt Eberflus' defense. Jacoby Brissett's 6 big plays vs the Cowboys had a combined EPA of 15.9. The Cowboys gave up 3 key 3rd downs in the 1st half, and a 2nd-and-forever as they hoped to close the 2nd half gap. Dallas hopes this won't be a get-right game for AZ... pic.twitter.com/233K0R1FcH — StopDropBinge (@StopDropBinge) October 31, 2026 Now he'll get to go against Christian Parker's defense, which is desperately trying to turn the corner. The club gave up three lengthy touchdown drives to the Eagles moribund attack last week, but did stop Philly on six of nine drives. Brissett offers more of a challenge than Tanner McKee, but the Cardinals should be an offense Dallas can continue to grow against. They'll get another reinforcement with the activation of safety PJ Locke, which should finally allow them to stop playing their weak-link reserves at the position and elevate the floor of the secondary. item.title: Ole Gunnar Solskjaer says he would have liked to stay in charge at Man United “forever”
item.description: Ole Gunnar Solskjaer says he would have liked to stay in charge at Man United “forever” Former Manchester United manager Ole Gunnar Solskjaer has revealed juicy details about his interview for the caretaker job earlier this year. The Norwegian and Michael Carrick both applied for the position following Ruben Amorim’s departure. The Englishman was chosen for the job, helped the Red Devils secure third place in the Premier League and ultimately bagged the full-time role. Unfortunately, Carrick has struggled to replicate that form this campaign, with his team now 17th in the league table after nine games, with just one win under the belt. The Englishman was expected to face the sack after Saturday’s 2-0 defeat at the hands of Chelsea at Stamford Bridge, but United continue to back him for now. With several managerial candidates tipped as possible replacements, Solskjaer has opened up on his former team-mate’s situation at the Theatre of Dreams. Solskjaer opens up on interviewing for caretaker position When asked by TV2 if he missed being United manager, Solskjaer responded: “Yes, well, sitting here like this… There were some fantastic moments, but everything in its own time. I do miss it, yes. I’d have liked to have stayed there forever, but life goes on.” The Norwegian went on to shed light on applying for the caretaker position earlier this year, which eventually went to Carrick. He said: “When I spoke to United, I spoke highly of Michael as well. ‘If you choose him, you’ll get a good man,’ I said. I think he did the same with me.” “Neither of us was desperate to get the job. We’d probably step up if they asked. At that particular time, the talk was of being an interim manager for the rest of the season.” Solskjaer insisted that had he taken the job, it would only have been until the summer, adding: “Going back to the way things were isn’t always such a good idea. Yes, I would have taken the job, but I hadn’t intended it to last any longer than until the summer. It was probably time for someone else to have a go.” Solskjaer rubbishes rumours of ‘demands’ Some reports suggested that Carrick was chosen ahead of Solskjaer because the Norwegian made greater demands than the former. However, the ex-United manager refuted those claims, stating: “No, that’s just nonsense!” “I had a nice chat with Jason Wilcox and Omar Berrada. We didn’t discuss contract length or anything like that. I was available if needed and didn’t make any demands. I gave my views on what needs to be done for the club to move forward. We had just a brief chat. There were no negotiations.” Solskjaer went on to back Michael Carrick to get things in order at Old Trafford, continuing: “Michael has what it takes to take this club forward. I think he’s the right man. He understands the club, understands the fans and knows what it takes.” The Norwegian also suggested that some of the challenges he faced during his time in charge at Old Trafford are yet to be addressed. item.title: Skip Bayless believes Malachi Toney’s presence makes it ‘hard to evaluate’ QB Darian Mensah
item.description: Photo by Chris Arjoon/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Skip Bayless has made a huge admission about the Miami Hurricanes quarterback Darian Mensah, stating that it was hard for the veteran analyst to evaluate him due to his superstar wide receiver teammate Malachi Toney. Mensah had a top game against Bill Belichick’s North Carolina, recording 274 passing yards and scoring 3 touchdowns. With the game hanging in the balance, Mensah connected with Malachi Toney on a 9-yard TD pass to give Miami a 38-28 lead. Although UNC responded with a touchdown of their own, Miami was able to hold on and grabbed a 38-35 win to maintain their unbeaten record. The QB-WR duo has been impressive for Miami, leading the best offensive unit in College Football. While Toney has received a lot of praise for his performances, Mensah has also been one of the best QBs, throwing at an 81.4% completion rate. Despite his accuracy and impact in Miami’s win against UNC, Toney’s brilliance continues to overshadow Mensah’s performances. Skip Bayless believes Malachi Toney’s brilliance makes it difficult to evaluate Mensah Malachi Toney has recorded 73 receptions for 1,027 yards while also scoring 13 touchdowns. Jeremiah Smith and Toney have been the wide receivers who have grabbed all the headlines. While Toney’s brilliance has helped him break several school records, Mensah has been putting up efficient performances and climbing up the draft rankings. He is expected to be one of the top QBs drafted in the 2027 NFL Draft. However, Bayless is not really ready to buy the hype around the Miami quarterback. “Malachi Toney is so good that it’s hard to evaluate Darian Mensah. I think he’s very good but Toney would make a lot of pretty good QBs look better than they should,” Bayless wrote on X. Mensah has thrown only 1 interception in 8 games, which is sensational for a college quarterback. In the NFL, efficiency is a key metric for a QB and so far Mensah has shown that he is highly reliable and can take care of the ball. The presence of Toney makes it easier for him, but Mensah is still a top quarterback and has proven that he can lead a top offence in CFB. The two teammates are going to be contenders for the Heisman Trophy, but it will be interesting to see who triumphs, as both have put up sensational numbers already. item.title: 3 things to buy, 1 thing to sell for the Cowboys vs Cardinals
item.description: Photo by Sam Hodde/Getty Images | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys finally put together a complete offensive performance in Philadelphia, and now they will try to carry that momentum into their matchup against the Arizona Cardinals. Javonte Williams delivered a career night against the Eagles, CeeDee Lamb found the end zone twice, and the Cowboys’ rushing attack finally looked like the unit it was supposed to be at the start of the season. The Cardinals have struggled defensively against the run, their offensive line is dealing with injuries, and the Cowboys are beginning to show some improvement against opposing rushing attacks. Concerns remain, particularly about Dallas’ tight end production and third-down defense. Here are some buy/sells for Week 8. Buy: Javonte Williams After waiting six weeks for Dallas to give him a substantial workload, Javonte Williams finally showed what he can do when the coaching staff commits to the ground game. His career performance against Philadelphia should earn him another healthy workload against Arizona. Williams rushed for 155 yards and a touchdown on 25 carries against the Eagles, averaging 6.2 yards per attempt. It was his best performance of the season and the most rushing yards by a Cowboys running back in nearly a decade. More importantly, it helped Dallas establish an offensive identity that had been missing during its consecutive losses to Tampa Bay and Green Bay. Through seven games, Williams has recorded 472 rushing yards and eight touchdowns on 110 carries, averaging 4.3 yards per attempt with eight rushing touchdowns so far in 2026. Arizona should provide another favorable opportunity. The Cardinals have allowed 126.4 rushing yards per game, ranking 24th in the league. Dallas finally showed what its offensive line can do when it moves downhill, and Williams should have opportunities to exploit that matchup. The biggest takeaway from Philadelphia was that Williams needs to be a focal point of this offense, not an afterthought. Schottenheimer should keep feeding him to achieve the balance he always talks about. Buy: CeeDee Lamb This is getting easy; this conversation comes up, and putting CeeDee Lamb in the mix is a no-brainer with how he’s performed so far this season. Lamb continues to remind everyone why he is the centerpiece of Dallas’ passing attack. Against Philadelphia, Lamb caught five passes for 74 yards and two touchdowns, giving Prescott another dependable option in the red zone. Over seven games, Lamb has caught 53 passes for 651 yards and six touchdowns. He leads the Cowboys in receiving yards and has been one of the team’s most consistent offensive weapons throughout the season. The Cardinals have struggled to consistently contain opposing offenses, and their secondary will have to account for both Lamb and George Pickens. item.title: The Daily: Red Wings Seeing Ghosts; Edvinsson Countdown Begins
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Red Wings let in five goals on just fifteen shots, and three goals in the third period to drop their afternoon matchup at home 5-4 to the St. Louis Blues to conclude October. Detroit managed to get contributions from all four lines and had the Blues offense shut down for much of the first half of the game but found themselves putting a lot of teaching moments on tape for the second half. “You can look at five on fifteen or whatever it was, and it’s not gonna show up real well in his number column, but you know, maybe you [get back] one of ’em, but don’t pin that on John Gibson by any means.” Head coach Todd McLellan said postgame. Still, the Red Wings, despite themselves sit at a just under .500 record to start the season, far better than many pundits had them before the year began. They’ll have four games over the next seven days to start November and every point in the standings is going to matter that much more, even if the team isn’t exactly expecting to make the playoffs this year. Helping things has been the emergence of Emmitt Finnie at center, including four points in his last five games as he’s taken over duties on the top line. However, with the turn of the calendar, the Red Wings now have just under a month to re-sign, or find a trade, for disgruntled defenseman Simon Edvinsson . Talk of what other teams could be offering has heated up around the league as attention shifts away from Larkin as the impasse grows between him and the team. Detroit must find Edvinsson a new contract, with the Red Wings or in a trade before Dec. 1 if they hope to not waste his season. Ken Holland in his last year as GM of the Red Wings selected Brattstrom with the 160th pick in the NHL entry draft in 2018. The Swedish netminder played in 50 games for the Red Wings AHL affiliate Grand Rapids Griffins but was unable to crack an NHL roster. item.title: Michigan Opens as MASSIVE Favorite vs. Michigan State
item.description: The Michigan Wolverines and Michigan State Spartans are preparing for their annual battle for the Paul Bunyan Trophy, but oddsmakers apparently aren’t expecting much of a battle. Despite Michigan’s struggles this season, the Wolverines have opened as a 13.5-point favorite over their in-state rivals ahead of Saturday’s showdown at Michigan Stadium. That’s a massive spread for one of college football’s fiercest rivalries, especially considering Michigan needed a late touchdown to escape Rutgers with a seven-point victory. But with Michigan State sitting at 2-6, the sportsbooks clearly believe the Wolverines have a significant advantage. Oct 31, 2026; Piscataway, New Jersey, USA; Michigan Wolverines quarterback Tommy Carr (14) celebrates after scoring a touchdown during the second half against the Rutgers Scarlet Knights at SHI Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Vincent Carchietta-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Michigan Favored by Nearly Two Touchdowns According to the opening betting lines shown Sunday morning, Michigan is favored by 13.5 points against the Spartans. Here’s a look at the numbers: Betting market Michigan Michigan State Point spread -13.5 (-122) +13.5 (+100) Moneyline -720 +530 Over/Under 40.5 points 40.5 points The numbers suggest Michigan is expected to win comfortably, with the moneyline making the Wolverines overwhelming favorites. A 13.5-point spread also means Michigan would need to win by at least 14 points to cover the opening number. The betting line is particularly interesting considering the Wolverines haven’t exactly been an offensive juggernaut in 2026. However, Michigan produced 427 total yards in Saturday’s 28-21 victory over Rutgers , with freshman quarterback Tommy Carr accounting for three touchdowns. That performance could give Michigan some much-needed confidence heading into rivalry week. Can Michigan State Pull Off a Shocking Upset? Michigan enters the matchup at 5-3 overall, while Michigan State has dropped six consecutive games and sits at 2-6. The Spartans are still searching for their first Big Ten victory of the season under head coach Pat Fitzgerald. However, anyone familiar with the Michigan-Michigan State rivalry knows that strange things can happen when these two programs meet. Michigan head coach Kyle Whittingham understands the importance of the matchup, recently identifying Michigan State as the Wolverines’ second-most-important rivalry . The Wolverines will also have the advantage of playing at Michigan Stadium, where the crowd should be electric for a primetime rivalry game. As we reported when the kickoff time was announced , Michigan and Michigan State will kick off Saturday, November 7, at 7:30 p.m. ET, with Peacock carrying the game. The Big Ten’s official announcement confirmed the primetime kickoff , setting the stage for another emotional battle for state bragging rights. For Michigan, Saturday represents an opportunity to build momentum and secure bowl eligibility.

item.title: 10 Takeaways: Mackenzie Blackwood Made the Big Saves When Calgary Tested Him (+)
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Calgary Flames didn’t generate a ton of offense against the Colorado Avalanche on Saturday night. But when they did, they made those chances count, creating some dangerous opportunities. The difference was Mackenzie Blackwood , who came up with several huge saves to keep the Flames at bay. The Avalanche controlling much of the shot share, they dictated play offensively, spending plenty of time in the Calgary zone and cycling the puck. Even with a multi-goal lead and what felt like a comfortable path to two points, Blackwood never let up. He stayed locked in until the final buzzer, delivering exactly what you want to see from your No. 1 goaltender. “I know they played last night, but you can tell they’re a younger group who will trade offense and defense for each other. They might give something up to get something,” Blackwood said. “So if you’re not really detail-oriented when you play them, it can be tough because you know they’re going to get their chances. “For me, you can’t take any team lightly. Whether we’re playing Carolina, Tampa, Dallas, you name it, right? Calgary Flames, they can freaking come in this rink and beat you any night. There are 32 good teams in the NHL, and onbany given night, if you’re not ready to go, they’ll beat you.” Also Read: Postgame Reaction: Avalanche’s Big Boys Came to Play Against Calgary 10 Takeaways 1. That’s Blackwood’s sixth consecutive start of good-to-great hockey. He’s 5-1-0 in that stretch and has not given up more than three goals in any game. He’s only surrendered three goals twice during this run. In that time, he has stopped 151 of 165 shots for a .915 save percentage. His five wins are tied for the second most in the league in that time. 2. We all remember the Toronto game two weeks earlier, when the Leafs barely had much to work with, but Blackwood didn’t make any big stops. That’s the performance that Bednar regularly brings up as one where he would’ve liked to see his goalie steal one. Blackwood had that type of night against the Flames. That robbery of a glove save on Matt Coronato with seconds remaining in the first period was spectacular. He also made a huge pad stop on Coronato again late in the second period in the crease. Those were just two of his highlight-reel stops. 3. Here’s what Bednar said postgame about his starting goalie. “Yesterday or the day before, I talked about the Toronto game, where we didn’t give up a lot of chances, but the ones we did were huge ones, and they went in the back of the net. That was the difference for me tonight. I thought we were doing the right things defensively, checking the right way, but we made some mistakes with the puck that, when we’re going one way and we turn the puck over and they’re coming the other way, it’s usually your best chance at creating a grade-A chance. They got a handful of them tonight, and he was awesome and made some huge saves for us.” 4. We really need a chant for Blackwood at Ball Arena. Th

item.title: Caption’s LLog: Sunday Photo Caption Contest (11/1/26)
item.description: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - MAY 24: Right fielder Luke Raley #20 of the Seattle Mariners slams his helmet during the 5th inning of the game against the Kansas City Royals at Kauffman Stadium on May 24, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Jamie Squire/Getty Images) | Getty Images Happy belated Halloween. I hope everyone had a happy holiday. I spent it at my mother-in-law’s house, eating chili, building a puzzle, and handing out candy to the trick-or-treaters of the neighborhood. The kids would knock, give their spiel, and then ask: “How many can I take?” I spent a good amount of the night considering whether this question was rude or polite. It made me laugh regardless. The enthusiasm for the answer (“take two please!”) seemed to wane throughout the evening as our bowl got picked over and Twizzlers were all that remained. It’s officially November. Daylight Savings Time has ended across the United States, meaning you have an extra hour this week to think of a good caption for our weekly contest. Last Week’s Winners Most Recs Personal Favorite Honorable Mention This Week’s Contest This week’s photo comes from a Mariners loss in Kansas City last May. It’s not exactly clear which play this comes from. The official caption says it was the fifth inning, but Luke Raley didn’t come up to bat in the fifth. He flew out in both the fourth and sixth innings. Regardless, after one of those fly outs, he spiked his helmet in frustration. I imagine he was frustrated, because it was pretty rare for Raley to make an out in those days. He hit .328/.403/.719 in May with eight homers as a platoon bat. His 215 wRC+ for the month was the sixth best by a Mariner this century. item.title: Bayern Munich CEO says not to rush into January signings following Der Klassiker injuries
item.description: Photo by Christina Pahnke - sampics/Corbis via Getty Images | Corbis via Getty Images Bayern Munich faced Borussia Dortmund and drew 2-2 at the Allianz Arena. The match brought bad news, with Bayern losing two players within the first half hour. Serge Gnabry and Ismael Saibari were both injured during the game, joining a long list of sidelined players. Later, Michael Olise also exited early, causing further concern. While having a large injury list is not necessarily a new problem for Bayern or club football in general, there is heightened anxiety regarding Bayern’s specific situation. Currently, the Bavarians have five out of their seven starting attackers injured. This is particularly worrying because those seven attackers cover just four positions. With fans calling for new signings in the January transfer window, CEO Jan-Christian Dreesen was asked whether the club might finally add players rather than assuming they are invincible to injuries. Dreesen responded by stating that it was too early for that discussion, citing players like Luis Diaz, Jamal Musiala, and Michael Olise, whose recovery timelines remain uncertain. “Lucho will be out for four to six weeks. He is making good progress and has resumed running training,” the CEO said, per Sky Sport and @iMiaSanMia . “Jamal will return. We also need to see what exactly is going on with Olise; it’s difficult to say at this stage. I think we shouldn’t rush into discussing these kinds of topics.” Naturally, fans are unlikely to take this well. Bayern soon face Atlético Madrid and several other tough opponents in both domestic and European competitions, alongside the ongoing risk of players picking up injuries on international duty. It may not be far-fetched for Bayern to consider reinforcing the full-back, defensive midfield, and wing positions, rather than continually assuming a full squad will be available outside of rare exceptions like this one. item.title: Alex de Minaur admits it’s ‘very annoying’ playing against Carlos Alcaraz after losing to him in the Vienna Open final
item.description: Carlos Alcaraz is the new Vienna Open champion. The Spaniard was in imperious form during Sunday’s showpiece event, triumphing 6-1, 6-4 in the Austrian capital. Alcaraz – who heavily praised De Minaur after the final – won 81 per cent of his first serve points, struck five aces and engineered eight break-point opportunities on his opponent’s serve. The 23-year-old now has a 15-2 record on the ATP Tour since returning from long-term injury at the end of August. Following the conclusion of Sunday’s final, Alcaraz and De Minaur vocalised their feelings. Alex de Minaur admits it is ‘very annoying’ to play Carlos Alcaraz “Alright. Let me start off with Carlitos. Well done to you, to your team,” De Minaur said during his post-match remarks. “It’s great to have you back on tour. I know all the fans appreciate it. I will say one thing though. It is very annoying to play against you. But as I said many times, you’re one of the good ones, one of the great guys on tour, so thank you very much, an amazing week. “As for myself, it’s been a great week. I feel very much at home here in Vienna. I play some of my best tennis, I would like to thank, you know, all the people that make it possible. “For the players is one of the great tournaments to come back to and we always look forward to coming back. So thank you for everything you do, to all kids, to the crowd, to everyone that makes this amazing tournament possible. Really appreciate it. “And last but not least, to my team, it’s been an interesting year, lots of highs, a couple lows, but I’m proud to be standing up here and still fighting. So, I’m excited for what’s left for this year and you know, hopefully I can continue pushing and have a longer year.” Alcaraz then took the microphone from the Australian and proceeded to praise his opponent’s play across the week in Vienna. De Minaur produced some of his best tennis to reach the final, beating Learner Tien, Matteo Berrettini and soon-to-be world number one Alexander Zverev. “I mean, obviously I’ve got to start with Alex, with an amazing week. You are always pushing forward, making steps always forward, always improving with your team. I’m just happy to see you, you know, every week, doing great things, keep pushing forward,” Alcaraz said. “So, great week, congrats for an amazing week. A couple of tournaments ahead of us for the rest of the season. Wish you always the best. So, yeah, congrats and keep going. Carlos Alcaraz’s path to the 2026 Vienna Open title R1: defeated Karen Khachanov 6-4, 7-6 R2: defeated Nikolos Basilashvili 6-1, 7-6 QF: defeated Tommy Paul 6-4, 7-6 SF: defeated Daniil Medvedev 6-4, 7-6 F: defeated Alex de Minaur 6-1, 6-4 “My team – it’s been an amazing, an amazing week for us. An amazing, emotional week as well. We had a great time on the court, but especially of the court, which makes me feel great every time I step on the court, feeling relaxed, feeling calm, feeling that I should enjoy more than stress myself, you know, playing, but

item.title: UConn men’s basketball season preview: The returnees
item.description: While it’s true that this year’s UConn men’s basketball team has an influx of new talent between the addition of impact transfers and a highly-touted freshmen class. With all of this turnover, the returning core from last year’s team that reached the national title will be relied upon to uphold the standards of quality, excellence and intensity that Dan Hurley has worked so hard to establish in Storrs. Hurley’s ability to bring Silas Demary Jr. and Braylon Mullins for one more run in the backcourt immediately made the thought of a fourth Final Four in five seasons a legitimate possibility. The continued ascension of Jayden Ross has been impressive, and his brother Jacob looks to carve out a role this season. And then there’s Solo Ball, one of the most accomplished players in program history, potentially waiting in the wings. The transfers and freshmen will help this team remain one of the top in the country, but if UConn is cutting down nets for title No. 7 in April, it will be because of the contributions from these players who are returning for another year with the Huskies. Silas Demary Jr. After a strong first season in Storrs where the Georgia transfer earned First Team All-Big East honors and established himself as one of the best two-way guards in the country, the senior is back for year two under Hurley with hopes for another deep tournament run. Demary Jr. averaged 10.1 points, 5.9 assists and 4.5 rebounds per game last season and shot 38.5 percent from three. He started last year slow as he adjusted to handling the complex UConn offense, but made history with a triple-double against Bryant and slowly start to look for his own shot instead of just serving as a facilitator. Demary Jr. embodies toughness and everything Hurley wants in his point guards. He’s tenacious on defense, using his quickness and length to disrupt opposing guards. He’s not afraid to get downhill and create contact offensively and will mix it up on the boards when needed. Despite suffering an ankle injury in the Big East Tournament that caused him to miss the Huskies’ first round win over Furman, he gutted out the rest of the tournament to make the Huskies’ championship run possible. Even while clearly not 100 percent, he tallied 18 assists to just six turnovers in five tournament games and flirted with a triple-double with seven points, seven assists and nine rebounds in the Final Four win over Illinois. This season, Demary Jr. is undoubtedly one of the best point guards in the country and has a full year of running the Huskies’ offense under his belt. He is unafraid to takeover games offensively and figures to be the heart and soul of this team now that Alex Karaban is gone. Braylon Mullins Early-season injuries and poorer-than-expected shooting numbers turned Mullins from a surefire one-and-done to a potential returnee following title game loss to Michigan. item.title: Former Bradford City chairman Richmond, 85, dies
item.description: Geoffrey Richmond oversaw Bradford's promotion to the Premier League in 1999 [Getty Images] The former chairman of Bradford City, Geoffrey Richmond, has died at the age of 85. Richmond helped oversee the Bantams' promotion to the Premier League in 1999, marking the first time the club had played in the top flight for 77 years. Announcing his death on Sunday, the club said Richmond had also "played an important role in the redevelopment" of its Valley Parade ground during his eight years as chairman. A City spokesperson added: "The thoughts of everyone at Bradford City AFC are with Geoffrey's family and friends at this difficult time." Richmond, who was born in Leeds and also served as chairman of Scarborough, took over at Valley Parade in 1994. The club was promoted to the First Division two years later after beating Notts County in a play-off final on its Wembley debut, before reaching the top flight in 1999. A famous David Wetherall header against Liverpool ensured survival on the final day of the season, but the club was relegated the following year after spending big on wages for players such as Benito Carbone and Stan Collymore. With the club in financial turmoil, Richmond left in 2002. Paying tribute on X, football reporter Alan Biggs described Richmond as "a larger than life figure in every sense" and "charismatic and controversial in equal measure". He added: "Can only speak from personal experience; provided many a story. Friendly, though could be cantankerous if you disagreed with him eg. over manager turnover." The Leeds-based New Rover Cricket Club, where Richmond was also a chairman and player, said he had played a "significant role" in its history. The club, based in Adel, said: "His contribution to New Rover, both on and off the field, will never be forgotten. "He was a valued member of our club family, and his commitment helped shape the club we are proud to be today." item.title: 'I never took a break.' Tireless effort took James Brooks to Bengals Ring of Honor
item.description: Waiting on the tarmac for an airport crew to de-ice their plane, one thing was clear to James Brooks and his San Diego Chargers teammates. “I said, 'I’m never coming back to Cincinnati because this place is too cold,’” Brooks said. “I had never experienced anything like that cold.” The Chargers were eager to get out of Cincinnati following the AFC Championship Game on Jan. 10, 1982, a contest that became known as the Freezer Bowl. The game at Riverfront Stadium was famous for windchills that dropped to around -60 degrees. The Bengals won, too. For the Chargers, a playoff run that started in thrilling fashion came crashing down in the Southwest Ohio cold. A week earlier, San Diego stunned head coach Don Shula’s Miami Dolphins , eliminating them in an overtime thriller at the Orange Bowl. The victory wasn’t the Super Bowl propellant they’d hoped it would be, and Brooks, whose rookie season ended with the loss to the Bengals in an unforgettable cold, simply wanted to go home. Less than three years later, Cincinnati became home for Brooks, but he said he couldn’t believe it when his agent called to tell him he’d be going back to the site of the Freezer Bowl via trade. “When they traded for me, really, I thought it was a joke. I was like, ‘really?’,” Brooks said. “I said, ‘I’m not sure I want to be in Cincinnati.’… (Bengals head coach) Sam Wyche called me and I’m like, I didn’t know who Sam Wyche was. I didn’t have any idea.” During an Oct. 27 interview with The Enquirer, Brooks said coming to Cincinnati was the best thing that ever happened to him. At 5-foot-10 and about 180 pounds during his playing days, Brooks might have been a diminutive figure on NFL fields. His play suggested otherwise, particularly in Cincinnati where from 1984 to 1991 he became one of the best running backs of his era, as well as the Bengals’ all-time leading rusher (6,447 yards). Multiple generations of Bengals fans are familiar with Ickey Woods, a second-round pick in the 1988 NFL Draft. That's thanks in part to the proliferation of Woods' signature touchdown celebration and modern commercials featuring the "Ickey Shuffle." Younger fans might not realize that Woods was drafted to eventually replace Brooks. At least that's how Brooks saw it, and with good reason. During Brooks' age-30 season in 1988, the 22-year-old Woods out-rushed him with 1,066 yards and 16 touchdowns to Brooks' 931 rushing yards and eight touchdowns. Unfortunately, injuries derailed Woods' career, and he was out of the game after the 1991 season. But for Brooks, he'd outlasted a competitor and maintained his significant place in the Bengals setup. As Woods' career looked to be winding down, the Bengals spent another second round NFL Draft pick on a running back, and this time it was Harold Green out of South Carolina in 1990. Facing another possible threat to his share of the Cincinnati offense, the prideful Brooks posted the third and final 1,000-yard rushing season of his career in Green's 1990 rookie

item.title: Spencer Anderson Embraces Role in Jumbo Package
item.description: Pittsburgh Steelers offensive lineman Spencer Anderson during a playoff game against the Houston Texans on Jan. 12, 2026. -- Ed Thompson / Steelers Now PITTSBURGH — After a sluggish start from their running game over the first couple weeks of the season, the Pittsburgh Steelers have adjusted and have hit the ground running ever since Jaylen Warren’s dominant performance against the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 3. And the running attack has continued as the Steelers dominated the New Orleans Saints on the ground in Paris last week, and head coach Mike McCarthy pulled a trick out of his hat when he used a familiar tactic that the 2025 Steelers offense often utilized by reintroducing the “Jumbo” package , using backup guard Spencer Anderson as a sixth offensive lineman. On 13 snaps out of the Jumbo package, they ran the ball 12 times for 77 yards and completed a pass for six yards, which is good enough for 6.4 yards per play. Despite McCarthy’s preference for a heavy passing attack, his decision to borrow from his predecessors and deploy the Jumbo package suggests that he is embracing the ‘bully ball’ football that this current roster excels at. Using heavier formations will make life more difficult for opposing defenses to contend with the one-two punch of Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle , who combined for 222 total yards on 36 touches against the Saints. When he was putting together the game plan for the Saints, McCarthy looked back to when he first accepted the head coaching job, when he was reviewing tape from last year’s team, and whether seeing the success that the team had played any part into the decision to include it in his game plan. “Absolutely,” McCarthy said. “I go back to when you get the job, the first thing you do is you sit down and start going through personnel. Spencer [Anderson], I was so impressed with him. It was a big part of the discussion of how we were trying to forecast him for where we felt he could play.” While it was last year’s coaching staff that created the blueprint for Anderson’s usage in the Jumbo package, McCarthy has also made it a part of his game plans while he was the head coach of the Dallas Cowboys. “I had a similar experience with Connor McGovern,” McCarthy said. “He’s up there in Buffalo now, and the whole time we were together in Dallas, it was like, ‘Hey, we’ve got to get him on the field.’ Is he a guard? Is he a center? He can play fullback. He can do all those things. So, when you have someone like Spencer with his unique talents, it gives you such great versatility.” After not installing the package over the summer both in OTAs and in training camp, the inclusion of it at the beginning of the week before the Saints game seemed to catch Anderson by surprise. “It was kind of out of the blue, if I’m being honest,” Anderson said. “I came in last week just getting breakfast at about six in the morning, and I walked past somebody, and they’re like ‘it’s back,’ and I’m like what are you talking about? item.title: Week 9 Report Card: Ducks get back on track vs. Northwestern
item.description: After the most tumultuous week in recent memory for the Oregon Ducks program, they emerged from the adversity and beat the No. 20 Northwestern Wildcats at Autzen Stadium. The Ducks came back from a 20-13 halftime deficit, winning by a final score of 34-26. The Wildcats had the upper hand in the first 30 minutes, with quarterback Aidan Chiles — a Oregon State and Michigan State transfer — dicing them up through the air and evading them with ease with his legs. By halftime, he had amassed over 200 total yards and two touchdowns, one passing and one rushing. He looked unstoppable, but that was until the Oregon defensed tightened the screws once they came back from the break. The Wildcats managed just six points in the second half, while Oregon's offense came alive despite the absences of star running backs Jordon Davison and Dierre Hill Jr. to injuries. In their place, true freshman running back Brandon Smith emerged with over 100 total yards and a touchdown, proving vital to the Ducks' offense in a relief outing. Quarterback Dylan Raiola looked sharp for the most part, surpassing 300 yards and three touchdowns through the air. Let's dive into this week's report card, featuring grades and analysis for every position group. But this week, with the coaching staff being the main topic since the Ducks last took the field, we evaluated the coaches first. Coaching Grade: B+ It was a tale of two halves for the coaches on both sides of the ball. In the first half, the offense led by playcaller Jay Johnson couldn't get out of first gear, settling for a pair of field goals in the red zone. The defense, meanwhile, had major trouble corralling Chiles and his top wide receiver, Griffin Wilde, who kept finding open space in the middle areas of the field. But some adjustments were made at halftime, as the Ducks outscored the Wildcats 21-6 in the final 30 minutes, with the offense flowing much more easily as they took shots down the field and the defense, led by Chris Hampton, closed the pocket in on Chiles, negating his creativity and play-making abilities. It was probably a "C-" performance from the coaches in the first half and an "A" in the second half, so a "B+" feels about right. Quarterbacks Grade: B+ There were still some scary moments, namely the fumble on the third play for Raiola, but he rebounded nicely and put together a 22-completion, 336-yard, three-touchdown game after weeks of abysmal play. Raiola is at his best when he can put touch on his throws, using his arm strength on deeper and midrange passes with little thinking to do. Where he struggles is on bullet passes, as he clearly puts too much pressure on himself and often short arms passes that should be easy completions. Play caller Jay Johnson schemed up deep and crossing routes for Raiola to stretch his arm out, helping out his quarterback in his first game in that role. item.title: Referee accidentally fractures college football player's leg
item.description: The incident happened at East Carolina Pirates' Dowdy–Ficklen Stadium [Getty Images] A referee accidentally fractured a college football player's leg during a bizarre incident in the first half of East Carolina Pirates' win against Temple Owls. East Carolina defensive back David Coleman Jr was standing on the field with team-mates in between plays, when an official ran in to address something near the 40-yard line. As the official approached the players from behind, he slipped and slid into Coleman Jr, who fell forward to the ground. Coleman Jr stayed on the turf, before eventually being helped from the field by two team members, who carried him so he did not have to put weight on his injured leg. East Carolina coach Blake Harrell later confirmed Coleman Jr had an X-ray at half-time which showed he fractured his fibula during the incident. "Our thoughts and our prayers are with him. But that's just one of those things. Kind of wild it happens, I'd never seen that from an official," said Blake. East Carolina won the game 17-9, with Coleman Jr recording one tackle during the match before he left the field. item.title: Spence 'very proud' to break WSL appearance record
item.description: Drew Spence was named Tottenham captain in the summer [Getty Images] Tottenham midfielder Drew Spence says it is a "very proud moment" to become the Women's Super League's all-time appearance record holder. Spence, 34, started in Tottenham's WSL game against Birmingham City on Sunday, making her 217th appearance in the competition. She overtook ex-Chelsea captain Millie Bright and could become the only outfield player at Tottenham to play 90 minutes in all of their WSL games this season. "I've been around for a while! I'm incredibly proud to be able to do that and it's not just a proud moment for me, but also for my family," Spence told BBC Sport. "It's [about] all the hard work that I put in throughout the years. When you're younger, you don't really think about these types of accolades. "It was all about winning trophies. Now it's happened, it's such a massive part of my career and something that I can be proud of to look back on. "I know the sacrifices - looking after yourself and making sure that you're available all the time. I know how hard it is to keep that motivation for so many seasons." Find interviews and extra content on the BBC Women's Football Weekly feed 'I'm in the best shape I've ever been' Spence has played her entire career in London, spending 14 years at Chelsea before making the move to Tottenham in 2022. She progressed from Arsenal and Fulham's academies and swapped nationalities from England to Jamaica in 2021. During her time at Chelsea she won five league titles and four FA Cup trophies as part of one of England's most successful squads. "She was a great team-mate, such a sweet soul off the pitch, but when she got on it, she was an absolute warrior," Chelsea midfielder Erin Cuthbert said. "Technically, she's got the brains and the skillset. She looked after me from the very beginning [although] she welcomed me to the club with a two-footed challenge! "She certainly deserves all the plaudits. To have that longevity is something I look up to. Now, she's a leader at Spurs." Spence was named Tottenham captain in the summer and has gone on to become a key figure under manager Martin Ho. In her first season at the club she played 22 games, more than in any campaign at Chelsea, and she has played every minute so far in 2026-27. "I feel like I'm probably in the best shape that I've ever been. I'm recovering quicker, I understand my body a lot more and the nutrition side of things has helped me," said Spence. "It's understanding what is right for me to recover and just little things. We have all those luxuries now which is amazing for the younger players." Drew Spence has overtaken Millie Bright as the WSL appearance record holder [Getty Images] Despite her achievements, Spence admits there are "regrets" from earlier in her career, when she wished she had understood how to prepare her body better. She believes that could have given her more consistency while at Chelsea but acknowledges it is a lesson that has helped her flourish

item.title: Hansi Flick: «Me gustó mucho lo que vi»
item.description: Hansi Flick: «Me gustó mucho lo que vi» El técnico alemán valoró la contundente victoria por 6-1 ante el Alavés, elogió las actuaciones de Lamine Yamal, Fermín López y Raphinha y destacó la respuesta del equipo tras las derrotas ante el PSG y el Real Madrid El FC Barcelona volvió a sonreír tras imponerse por 6-1 al Deportivo Alavés en el Spotify Camp Nou. El conjunto dirigido por Hansi Flick ofreció una gran actuación ofensiva y respondió de la mejor manera posible a los últimos resultados negativos. Después del encuentro, el entrenador alemán se mostró muy satisfecho con el rendimiento de sus jugadores y aprovechó la ocasión para celebrar sus 100 victorias al frente del Barça . «Estoy extremadamente satisfecho. Dominamos la primera parte y creamos ocasiones aprovechando los espacios. Me gustó mucho lo que vi. Hemos jugado bien» , explicó Flick en rueda de prensa. El técnico destacó especialmente el control del partido frente a un rival que planteó dificultades defensivas y buscó hacer daño mediante transiciones rápidas. «El Alavés defendió muy bien, tenía muchos jugadores atrás. Sabíamos que harían buenas transiciones, pero controlamos el partido y conseguimos atacar los pequeños espacios que nos dejaron» , añadió. Frenkie De Jong y Brian Fariñas fueron las novedades en el once blaugrana. Foto: FC Barcelona Flick destaca la actuación de Lamine, Fermín y Raphinha Uno de los aspectos más positivos del encuentro fue la respuesta de los jugadores ofensivos azulgranas. Lamine Yamal y Raphinha firmaron sendos dobletes , mientras que Fermín López volvió a destacar con un gol y una actuación determinante en ataque. Flick se mostró especialmente satisfecho con el rendimiento de los tres futbolistas, sobre todo después de las derrotas ante el PSG y el Real Madrid. Sobre Lamine, el entrenador explicó que había hablado con él durante el descanso y destacó que había recuperado la confianza en los duelos individuales. «Era importante que tuviera algo de descanso y ha estado fantástico. Era lo que quería ver, también de Fermín y Raphinha tras las dos derrotas» , señaló el técnico alemán. El entrenador también explicó la sustitución de Pedri en el descanso , argumentando que el centrocampista tenía una tarjeta amarilla y que no era necesario asumir riesgos. De Jong como central y el debut de Brian Fariñas Las numerosas bajas en defensa obligaron a Flick a buscar soluciones alternativas para configurar el once inicial. Una de ellas fue situar a Frenkie de Jong en el centro de la defensa , mientras que Brian Fariñas debutó con el primer equipo como lateral derecho . El técnico azulgrana agradeció la predisposición de ambos futbolistas y elogió especialmente al joven canterano por su rendimiento y su trabajo diario. «Pregunté a Frenkie y a Brian si podían jugar en esa posición y les agradezco su trabajo. Brian merecía jugar por su profesionalidad en los entrenamientos. Ha jugado a buen nivel y se ha compenetrado muy bien con Lamine» , afirmó. Sobre la posibilidad

item.title: The Morning After: Torture Chamber
item.description: IOWA CITY, IA - OCTOBER 31: Tight end Addison Ostrenga #87 and offensive lineman Jack Dotzler #71 of the Iowa Hawkeyes carry the Heartland Trophy off the field after the match-up against the Wisconsin Badgers at Kinnick Stadium on October 31, 2026 in Madison, WI. (Photo by Matthew Holst/Getty Images) | Getty Images Let’s just say it right up front – Kirk Ferentz has Luke Fickell and Wisconsin in the torture chamber. And there is no escape in sight. Since Wisconsin’s last win in this series, in 2021 – a football lifetime ago – the Badgers have scored a grand total of two (2) touchdowns and 26 points against Iowa. They scored a touchdown late in the first half of the 2022 game, and early in the fourth quarter of the 2024 game. Two in five meetings. The margin the last five years is 148-26. Since that late 2024 touchdown, Iowa’s on an 81-0 run against the Badgers. “81-0 run” really rolls off the tongue. They managed to go eight (8) quarters without scoring a single point against the Hawks. Eight quarters . Two games! Iowa with consecutive shutouts against the Badgers – what a time to be alive! Wisconsin hasn’t been shut out in consecutive games against an opponent since Michigan from 1977-1980. Neither team’s done this in the series before. It’s crazy just how much Iowa’s in their heads. This feels a bit like the mid-90s, when no matter how good Wisconsin was, they couldn’t beat Iowa. Just couldn’t do it. And that’s part of what makes this so shocking. Wisconsin dipped some as a program, but they feel like they’re improving and back on a solid trajectory under Fickell. They (mostly) look the part again. The USC win was impressive and takes on added weight given the Trojans just defeated Ohio State. Say what you will about Penn State, but it takes a big pair to win in Happy Valley. But then you watch this and wonder if Fickell heads back to the hot seat in Madison. They do not have the answer against Iowa right now. Nowhere close to the answer against the Hawkeyes. And this is an Iowa team coming off last week’s disappointing Minnesota showing, down their starting running back, and generally searching for answers. And that game was over in the first 10 minutes of the first quarter. Iowa completely dominated this game, from start to finish. Watching yesterday, I wonder how there was ever a quarterback battle in Iowa City. Hank Brown had easily his best game at this level. His 190 passing yards in the first half were the most by an Iowa quarterback in the first half of a game since Nate Stanley against Illinois in 2019 . He was in total command of the Iowa offense, pushing all of the right buttons, hitting throws from the start. His early 45-yard completion to DJ Vonnahme set the tone out of the gate. The drive didn’t end with a touchdown – Kade Pieper went the wrong way on third down – but Iowa immediately got it going on a day that looked dreary in eastern Iowa. Even throws on which Brown was hit, he was getting it on target. He was in total control,

item.title: Bob Trumpy played by his own rules on route to Bengals Ring of Honor
item.description: Bob Trumpy had a knack for getting his way, whether he was convincing Cincinnati Bengals coaches to run an off-script deep route or spearheading the movement to beat the heat during training camp at Wilmington College. The latter required a little ingenuity. During grueling summer training camps in Wilmington, players weren't allowed to have window air conditioners in their dorm rooms. Trumpy and roommate Bob Johnson, the team's first-ever draft pick , found a workaround that would benefit everyone. Trumpy and Johnson had a friend in Glendale, Melna Burchenal , who owned a window unit that wasn't technically an air conditioner. They brought it to Wilmington, where its power surge caused the lights in the dorm to dim. Williams: Cincinnati Bengals remain model of inconsistency More: Here's how Bengals' second half vs Ravens made NFL history More: 'That's who we have to be.' Bengals show promise in comeback win vs. Ravens "It was huge. It didn't look anything like a modern air conditioner," Johnson said. "Trumpy said, 'I got it. We're gonna go in there and tell them it's an air cooler.' I made Trumpy put it in the window all by himself because I was not gonna be involved." It first passed a bed check inspection from linebackers coach Vince Costello and later from Bengals founder and head coach Paul Brown. The humid halls of Wilmington College would never be the same. "Everyone had one," Johnson said. "That was completely from Trumpy's chutzpah." That is arguably one of Trumpy's biggest contributions to the Bengals, but his stellar 10-year career on the field is why the late tight end will be inducted into the Bengals Ring of Honor alongside James Brooks on Sunday, Nov. 1. More: Bengals icon Bob Trumpy was a radio pioneer, 'gentle giant' and 'godfather' Bob Trumpy's long road to Cincinnati Trumpy's knack for finding a way around the rules was part of a larger personality that made him memorable. On the field, the same confidence helped make him one of the most dangerous offensive weapons on the Bengals' early teams. Trumpy was one of the 31 selections by the Bengals on the final day of the 1968 AFL-NFL Draft, going in the 12th round. He was a travel-weary rookie after an unconventional path to professional football included playing at Illinois, Glendale College in California and Utah before a six-month stint in the U.S. Navy during the Vietnam War. Before joining the Bengals, he had quit his job as a collection agent in Compton, California, after someone pointed a gun at him on a porch, and Trumpy began building Shasta travel trailers, according to longtime Cincinnati sportswriter and broadcaster Chick Ludwig, a former Bengals beat reporter for the Dayton Daily News. item.title: FG launches USSD service to help Nigerians access loans without internet [How to apply]
item.description: The Federal Government has launched a new USSD-based credit service, SPARK, designed to help Nigerians access loans and build formal credit histories using basic mobile phones. The product, introduced by the Nigerian Consumer Credit Corporation (CREDICORP), targets Nigerians, particularly first-time borrowers who have limited or no credit history. Interested Nigerians can dial *347*333# on their mobile phones to access the service without requiring a smartphone or internet connection. According to CREDICORP, SPARK is designed to simplify access to consumer credit while helping beneficiaries establish repayment records that could improve their credit profiles and open up further financial opportunities. “By establishing repayment records through responsible borrowing, beneficiaries can progressively improve their credit profiles and create pathways to greater financial opportunities,” the corporation said. It added that the product is expected to become more widely available to Nigerians before the end of 2026. Why FG introduced SPARK The product was unveiled at CREDICORP’s ‘CREDICORP for All’ showcase in Aba, Abia State, where the corporation highlighted affordable credit opportunities for more than 1,000 residents. The event brought together beneficiaries, participating financial institutions, local vendors and government representatives to demonstrate how consumer credit could support businesses and improve livelihoods. Activities included credit-access demonstrations for market women and traders, presentations on the YouthCred initiative for young Nigerians, and the showcasing of credit-backed tricycles for transport operators. The event also featured locally assembled tricycles made available on credit through CREDICORP’s Securing Consumer Access for Local Enterprises (S.C.A.L.E.) initiative. CREDICORP Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer, Uzoma Nwagba, said the initiative was designed to make consumer credit accessible beyond traditional financial institutions. “Consumer credit should not be a privilege reserved for a few. It should be an opportunity available to every working Nigerian,” he said. He added, “Today in Aba, Abia State, in Nigeria’s South East, we are demonstrating what that means in practical terms: credit for market women, a financial head start for young people, productive assets for transport operators, and with SPARK, a simple way for Nigerians to begin building their credit histories. This is how we make credit work for the people.” Chinenye Mba-Uzoukwu, chief principal to Abia State Governor Alex Otti, said the state government was creating an environment where responsible consumer credit and enterprise could thrive. “Under Governor Alex Otti’s leadership, Abia State is putting the conditions in place for businesses to grow, investments to flourish and responsible credit to reach more of our people,” Mba-Uzoukwu said, representing the governor at the event. “By strengthening the enabling environment for enterpris

item.title: Planetary defense: How military and civil satellites are watching fireballs to help keep Earth safe from space rocks
item.description: null It came from outer space, exploding high above the South Atlantic off the coast of Argentina. That April 1 event — an incoming meteor , also termed a bolide — was observed by both U.S. space-based military and civil sensors. Hush-hush U.S. government satellite sensors detected the speedy fireball cutting through our atmosphere. The object's brightness peaked at an altitude of nearly 60 miles (90.5 kilometers) over the South Atlantic. That dazzling spectacle was also caught by the National Atmospheric and Oceanic Administration's GOES-E and Europe's Meteosat Third Generation (MTG) Imager-1 satellite. Those two independent spacecraft in geostationary orbit detected the bolide via onboard lightning imagers. This skyfall show is among a number of recent episodes that spotlight the value of combining multi-sensor data to not only portray fireball dynamics but also to help appreciate human-caused space debris impacts, as well as strengthening planetary defense knowhow. Hovering in a fixed position high above Earth's equator, the Meteosat Third Generation mission is designed to deliver a rapid stream of data for enhanced weather forecasting. Its Lightning Imager offers a completely new capability for European meteorological satellites, including bolide detection. (Image credit: ESA/Mlabspace) Catastrophic fragmentation Take, for instance, another extraterrestrial incident. In this case, an April 24, 2025 fireball over south-central Alaska yielded one of the most densely recorded "seismoacoustic" datasets ever obtained for a nature-made bolide en route to busting up. A network of 37 seismic stations, 16 single infrasound sensors, and four infrasound arrays recorded 30 ballistic and multiple fragmentation arrivals. All this was complemented by Doppler weather radar detections of falling meteorites and independent optical video observations. Now, toss in for good measure yet another encounter. A roughly 12-foot-wide (3.7 meters) space rock plowed through Earth's atmosphere over northwest Queensland, Australia, on May 20, 2023, accompanied by a raucous round of sonic booms. And U.S. government space-based sensors caught the fall . Researchers later determined that the object underwent catastrophic fragmentation, producing one of the 20 most energetic events reported by NASA's Center for Near-Earth Object Studies (CNEOS) since 1988 and the most energetic seen over Australia. It was equivalent to the explosion of a 7.1-kiloton bomb. An April 24, 2025 fireball event over south-central Alaska. This illustration is a detection map showing a regional seismo-acoustic network in south-central and interior Alaska. Only stations with available data during the fireball event are shown. Green stations denote sensors with detections. (Image credit: Scamfer, L. T., et al.)
